title: Why peas and mint Works So Well Together
flavorProfile: The pairing balances sweet, fresh peas with bright, herbaceous mint, creating a savory-sweet-umami profile. Peas contribute a gentle sweetness and a hint of umami from their amino acids, while mint adds a cool, slightly sweet aroma and a touch of acidity that lifts the overall flavor, resulting in a harmonious, refreshing taste.
nutritionalSynergy: Mint is rich in vitamin C, which enhances the absorption of non-heme iron found in peas. The antioxidant polyphenols in mint also help protect the carotenoids in peas, improving bioavailability of fat-soluble vitamins. Together they create a synergistic effect that boosts iron uptake and antioxidant activity.
prepTechniques: Blanch fresh peas in boiling water for 2 minutes, then transfer to an ice bath to preserve color and texture.
Finely chiffonade fresh mint leaves, reserving a few whole leaves for garnish.
Toss the cooled peas with mint, a drizzle of extra-virgin olive oil, lemon zest, and a pinch of sea salt.

faq.a: Store the pea-mint mixture in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze in a single layer on a baking sheet, then transfer to a freezer bag for up to 2 months.

If fresh peas are unavailable, frozen peas work well after thawing. For mint, you can use fresh basil or a small amount of chopped parsley for a similar herbaceous note, though the flavor will differ.
